label: verify-bm-resin-water-uptake-data

claims.claim: Flexible 80A Resin V2 gains +8% mass and +3% volume after 1 day and +9% mass and +7% volume after 1 week in deionized water (ASTM D471 slab), unlike the under-1% cube figures for other Formlabs resins.
claims.source_says: Deionized Water: 1 day -26 +8% +3% 94% 89%; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88%. 'Rectangular slabs, used for hardness, mass, and volume change, are evaluated immediately after wiping dry'
claims.note: The V2 numbers reproduce exactly from the PDF word coordinates, but 'other Formlabs resins are under 1%' is too broad because the same record lists Elastic 50A V1 at 2.3% in water.

claims.claim: Elastic 50A V1 prints both size and weight change for a 24 h cube: in solvents size/weight is 0.44 to 0.52, and in water weight is +2.3% with size only '<1%'.
claims.source_says: Water: size '<1', weight '2,3'. Acetone 19,3/37,3; isopropyl 13,3/25,6; butyl acetate 18,2/39,6; xylene 20,4/46,6; Skydrol 5 9,9/21,7.
claims.note: The ratios work out to 0.517, 0.520, 0.460, 0.438 and 0.456, so the 0.44 to 0.52 range reproduces for the major solvents.

claims.claim: No independent measurement of linear hygroscopic strain exists for a Formlabs resin; the nearest independent data are Denture Base OP sorption values that disagree 2.4-fold (17.86 ug/mm3 at 48 h vs 7.53 at 7 d) and a Form 3 Clear Resin null length result.
claims.source_says: Gad: Formlabs water sorption 'Before ... 17.86(0.83)', 48 h at 37 C. Izzettinoglu: 'Wsp-DW 7,53 ± 1,74(8,08)', 7 days. Radic: 'side lengths ... remained 4.80 cm ... within the ± 0.15 mm manufacturing tolerance'.
claims.note: All three data points and the 2.4x ratio (17.86/7.53 = 2.37) are real, but the 'no measurement exists' part cannot be shown by these sources, and the two papers used different disc thicknesses and protocols.

claims.claim: Water diffusivity in printed methacrylate photopolymer is of order 1e-12 m2/s or lower (0.85e-12 reported; about 2.6e-13 on recheck), with sorption still rising at 14 days (11.1 to 39.8 ug/mm3), so layers of 0.4 mm and up need days to equilibrate.
claims.source_says: 'D = 1.02–1.15 × 10−12 m2/s for milled and 0.85 × 10−12 m2/s for printed materials'; resin IV wsp median 11.1 (24 h) to 39.8 (14 days).
claims.note: The reported D and the 11.1 to 39.8 medians match, and my own half-time estimate gives about 2.6e-13 (half of 39.8 first reached near 53 h), but the paper's 1 mm DLP plates are non-Formlabs, and 'days for 0.4 mm' is an extrapolation rather than something the paper states.

overall: The raw numbers in all four key claims reproduce from the original sources. Two claims are fully checkable and match. The Flexible 80A V2 claim overreaches in its comparison to other resins, the Denture Base OP claim rests on an absence statement no source can support, and the diffusivity claim extrapolates beyond the 1 mm plates the paper tested.
